title: Capturing and attack

D0.outcome: Says that you capture by moving onto an enemy piece, which leaves the board, and that a piece is attacked when the enemy could capture it next move.

D1.outcome: When told 'capture something safe', finds a capture that wins an undefended piece, and names which of its pieces attack a given enemy piece.

D2.outcome: In mixed positions tells a free piece from a defended one, and does not count a nearby enemy piece as a defender when it cannot capture on that square.

D3.outcome: Plays out a chain of captures and recaptures on one square in the head and says the net result in points.

misconceptions: A capture you can make is always a good capture.
conditions: Capturing is landing on an enemy piece; the captured piece leaves the board.
A capture wins material when the piece is undefended, or when what you take is worth more than what you can lose back.
contrasts: The same capture is free when the piece is undefended and loses material when it is defended and the capturing piece is worth more.
A nearby enemy piece that cannot capture on the square does not defend it.
